title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: Frobenius-class rho with lazily evaluated steps (prefix-product trie, 4,964-instruction key kernel, one full multiplication per six steps)

claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity P in G1 and uniform z in GT, the algorithm in proof.md (compute g=e(P,Q0) for the fixed G2 generator Q0; solve z=g^x by distinguished-point Pollard rho on the 12-element Frobenius classes of GT in the van Oorschot-Wiener trail form with exponents recovered by replay, as in the parent package gt-dprestart-replay, but with the multiply-only R=24 adding walk evaluated lazily: each walk keeps an explicit base y and a node of a precomputed prefix-product trie of depth 6 over the 288 twisted multipliers, its current element is y*Pi_node, the class key of that element is computed from the w^1 coefficient c_1(y*Pi_node)=sum_k y_k gamma_k(Pi_node) by the 4,964-instruction straight-line kernel lazy.s (1,561 for root.s at the root), and the base is made explicit by one 14,402-instruction multiplication mul.s every sixth step; multiplier index (bits 0..63), distinguished-point bits (64..149, theta=2^-86) and 112-bit fingerprint (150..261) are read from the key minimum K; every closure inside a trail is caught by the 2-cycle test, a 64-step checkpoint or a doubling (Brent) checkpoint and escaped by squaring the class whose key is smaller with the distinguished-point bits masked (the full key breaks a tie); a walk is restarted after A=120/theta counted steps without a distinguished point; a pre-debit 192-bit work meter, report log (cap 2^55), restart cap 2^20, matcher with a pair budget of 2^4, sampler as in the parent; output Q=[x]Q0, Q=infinity exactly when z=1, and verify e(P,Q)=z) succeeds, in the ideal model, with probability at least 0.39 using at most 2^124.210 total dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents (C=20,000) on every run, including setup (the table and the 2^49.02-leaf trie, one unit per node), pairings, walk starts and fresh starts, distinguished-point handling, escapes, detection delay, stuck-walk restarts at their worst case, matching (sort, duplicate removal, replays and pair checks), output and verification. A complete block of six steps is charged 41,845 instructions (root step 1,735, lazy step 5,138, lazy step with the flush 19,558; 174 of every-step work each), c=41,845/120,000 (0.348708333...) units per step, and a partial block less per step; fruitless-cycle waste is charged as eps=0.030335 (1.25 times the H2 model: 2-cycles at 1/288 per step, other cycles up to length 64 at 6.17e-5, the doubling checkpoint's closures at 3.22e-4, longer useless walks below 2^-108.79 per step). The ledger is 2^124.20923 and 2^124.210 is the least thousandth above it; a run has at most 2^125.730 iterations because every block of iterations, with the escape or report that ends it, is charged at least c per iteration. Peak memory is below 2^62 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^49.06 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. The success bound relies on three heuristics, none proven: H1, the random-mapping heuristic for rho walks with the conservative correction 1/(1-1/R), used at useful images only, with structural returns into a trail's current segment carved out (fruitless closures, charged in eps and escaped, never counted as collisions), and pairwise (two given useful images coincide with probability at most 2/N, twice the random-mapping rate; the enlarged N' is used only in the success law, never in a union bound), never conditioned on the history; H2 models bits 0..261 of K as a random function of the class, and the multiplier indices and the frame of each element arriving at a fresh class as independent uniform; and H1+, that the run's realized waste stays within t=2 times its H2 rate, whose cost is computed as the drop of the collision law from S to S_tol=2^125.66024 (loss 0.0106656). The report, restart and pair caps are bounded by Markov's inequality (tails 2.53e-5, 8.1e-8, 2.1e-7), and a detection lemma bounds a stuck trail by 2^-43.28. Model success is 0.4014 at S=2^125.68551; after the H1+ tolerance loss and the computed losses of proof.md section 4 (restart-cap worst case 1.4232e-4 as a fraction of S, the three Markov tails, detection on the colliding trails, collision inside one trail, ties (including a masked-key tie at the minimum of a doubling escape's closure), the closure-compare and stuck-trail-merge items, beta^1 = beta^2, sampler; sum 0.0108345) success is at least 0.39056 (computed 0.3905655). The 0.39 bound is conditional on H1+: it falls by 0.0137 per unit of t, so it still holds for any t up to 2.04 and fails at t=3. The heuristics are supported by the emulated kernels, the production lazy walk run step by step against an eager walk in the real BLS12-381 GT with distinguished points, records, fresh starts, a 2-cycle escape and replay of every record (an extended run recorded in evidence.md, input r2_steps 12000, adds a 12,000-step walk at R=2 that exercises the 2-cycle, 64-step and doubling escapes), statistics of the bits of K on production classes, and a registered toy-field census of the complete algorithm (census 5, 3,600 runs with the success threshold at the model point 0.4014 and the masked-key escape rule: success 0.4308, Wilson 95% lower end 0.4147; waste 0.91 of the H2 rate). No production-size run is claimed.

experiments.purpose: Part A: BLS12-381 GT identities (Frobenius, the 12-key formula against explicit conjugates, canonical representative, orders, Granger-Scott). Part K: generate the four straight-line kernels in memory and run them in the shipped emulator on real GT elements against a big-integer reference (counts 14,402 / 6,777 / 4,964 / 1,561 on every call). Part C: the production lazy walk (R=24, trie depth 6, 2-cycle test, 64-step checkpoint and doubling checkpoint; an extended run with input r2_steps 12000, recorded in evidence.md, adds a 12,000-step walk at R=2 that takes 2-cycle, 64-step and doubling escapes; the declared input sets r2_steps 0 so the run finishes in about 10 s) in the real GT with every key from emulated root.s/lazy.s and every flush and escape from emulated mul.s/sqr.s, with distinguished points at a test density, records, fresh starts, compared at every step with an eager walk, and every record replayed from its start pair to the same fingerprint with its canonical pair verified. Part G: statistics of the bits of K read by the rule on production classes. Part B: the complete algorithm (trails, report log, heapsort matcher, replay, escapes, meter) in toy fields, with the success metric in the ledger's step equivalents. Part E: pair-collision law. Part F: exact fruitless-cycle bounds at R=24. Part D: the ledger, caps, budget inequality and claim on integers. Part S: the bounded sampler; flags_check.py: multiword compares under AArch64 NZCV. No production costs are measured by running the attack.
